_readme: Hand-written gold sets, one per extractor, so an F1 drop points at which pass regressed.
Entities are matched on name+type. Relations on source+predicate+target.
Edit these freely - they are the specification the extractors are scored against.

cases.why: One small module exercising four AST edge kinds: a resolved path-alias import, an exported function, a dynamicRpc-wrapped invoke, and a read-only supabase chain.
notes: Scored by provenance: only facts whose file_path is this file.
The imports edge asserts module RESOLUTION: '@/services/types' must land on src/services/types.ts. The external '@supabase/supabase-js' import must produce nothing.
invokes comes from the dynamicRpc(client, "get_yeast_lineage_root", args) wrapper - argument index 1, not 0. A regression to plain .rpc() matching loses this edge.
reads_from, not writes_to: the fluent chain is .select().eq().single(), no write method. A chain-walk regression flips this.

Deliberately absent: a calls edge to src/services/types.ts#dynamicRpc. Direct calls to imported identifiers resolve to the local import specifier (alias not dereferenced), so the AST pass emits none; the invokes edge carries the semantic fact. If alias dereferencing is ever added, add the calls edge here in the same commit.

cases.why: Three RLS policies with no user_has_permission() call, plus an ALTER TABLE that must NOT produce a creates edge.
notes: Scored by provenance: this lists only what the SQL pass attributes to THIS file.
The three RLS_POLICY nodes and their `protects` edges are attributed to supabase/live-catalog.snapshot.txt, which is authoritative for policy->table. They are real, just not this file's contribution.
No PERMISSION entity: these policies gate on auth.uid() and a key NOT LIKE filter, not user_has_permission().
No creates edge to system_settings or user_preferences - the migration only INSERTs into and ALTERs them. That absence is the assertion this case exists to make.

cases.why: The webhook case. Under the tightened LLM schema this file yields exactly one boundary fact; everything else in it belongs to the AST pass.
notes: Deliberately excluded: verifyWebhookSignature, checkReplayWindow, the ingest RPCs, square_sync_log.
Those are FUNCTION/DB_FUNCTION/TABLE facts the AST and SQL passes already own exactly.

cases.why: A rules document. It describes conventions rather than naming a specific system entity, so the correct answer is nearly empty - which is the point.
notes: This case exists to catch over-extraction. A pass that invents entities here is hallucinating structure from prose.
docs/spec/architecture.md is referenced by this file, but a doc-to-doc citation is not a documented_in edge - open question, see the report.
